name: Aangan Homestay
description: A calm, photo-led site for a family homestay in the hills: rooms and rates, a day at the house, food, walks, how to get there and a booking form.

Arrivals any time before dark
Dinner at 19:00

pages.title: Home
pages.seoTitle: Aangan Homestay, Ghandruk: a Gurung home facing Annapurna South
pages.seoDescription: Four rooms in a stone house in upper Ghandruk, with dinner and breakfast cooked by the family. From Rs 4,400 a night for two. Mountain views from every window.

props.title: A stone house in Ghandruk, with Annapurna South at the window
props.text: Four rooms in our family home at the top of the village. Dal bhat at seven, milk tea at dawn, and the mountain turning pink while you drink it.

image.alt: Our stone house at dusk, with Annapurna South lit pink behind it

props.eyebrow: Four rooms · Dinner and breakfast included · 1,940 metres

props.quote: My husband’s father carried these roof slates up from the river on his back. We kept the roof, the walls and the fire. We added hot water and good beds.
props.name: Dil Maya Gurung
props.detail: Host, and cook of the dal

image.alt: A small timber-lined room with a window framing the mountains

props.heading: Every room faces the mountain
props.body:
Pine-lined walls, thick cotton quilts and a window that looks straight up the Modi Khola to Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Two rooms share a bathroom; two have their own.

The hot water is from the solar panel on the roof, and from the kitchen fire on cloudy days.

props.heading: Ghandruk, from our roof
props.intro: The village is a stone staircase of Gurung houses. We are near the top, five minutes above the museum.

image.alt: Slate-roofed houses of Ghandruk on the hillside
Last light on Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre
Cloud rolling over the village rooftops
The village roofs and lit windows at night
Two stone houses with slate roofs beside a field

props.heading: A day at Aangan
props.intro: Nothing is scheduled except dinner. This is what most guests end up doing.

image.alt: Milk tea being poured into a glass

items.title: Tea on the terrace
items.text: Aama puts a glass of milk tea in your hand and points at the mountain. On clear mornings the sun reaches the summit about twenty minutes before it reaches us.

items.title: Breakfast
items.text: Gurung bread with honey from the hives below the school, eggs, and more tea.

items.label: Daytime
items.title: Walk, or don’t
items.text: Up to Komrong Danda, across to Landruk, round the museum, or a book in the sun on the roof.

items.title: Dal bhat by the fire
items.text: Everyone eats together in the kitchen. Seconds arrive whether you ask or not.

props.heading: Rooms and rates
props.intro: Per night, for the room, with dinner and breakfast for everyone in it. Children under six stay free.

plans.name: Twin room
plans.note: Two single beds, shared bathroom with a hot shower.

plans.name: Double room with bathroom
plans.note: The corner room, with the widest window.

plans.name: Family attic
plans.note: Sleeps four under the roof beams, with its own bathroom.

image.alt: A brass plate of rice, dal and vegetable curries on a woven dhaka cloth

props.heading: Dinner is dal bhat, and there is always more
props.body:
Rice, black dal, whatever is green in the garden, potatoes with timur, and a pickle that changes with the month. Chicken on request, a day ahead.

We cook on a clay stove with wood from the community forest. If you want to learn, pull up a stool; Aama teaches while she cooks.

props.heading: Walks from the door
props.intro: Times are at an easy pace, there and back.

items.title: Komrong Danda at sunrise
items.text: A steep path through rhododendron to the ridge above the village. Take a torch and a jacket.

items.title: The Gurung Museum
items.text: Old tools, clothes and a real kitchen, in a house like ours. Open from ten.

items.title: Across to Landruk
items.text: Down to the Modi Khola bridge and up the other side. Lunch in Landruk, jeep back if your knees ask.

items.title: Tadapani forest
items.text: Moss, stone steps and langur monkeys, on the trail towards Ghorepani.

props.heading: Getting to Ghandruk
props.address: Upper Ghandruk, ward 11, five minutes above the Gurung Museum
props.hours:
Pokhara to Kimche by jeep, about 2 hours 30 minutes
Kimche to our door on foot, about 1 hour
props.note: Ask anyone for Dil Maya’s house. From the museum, climb the stone steps and turn left at the prayer wheel. We send someone down to Kimche to carry bags if you tell us your jeep time.

items.a: Kartik to Magh, most mornings. In spring the rhododendrons are out but haze comes up by ten. In the monsoon you may see nothing for days, and then everything at once.

Ghandruk is inside the Annapurna Conservation Area. Foreign visitors need an entry permit from the Tourism Board office in Pokhara or Kathmandu; it is checked at Kimche. Nepali visitors pay a small fee at the checkpoint.
Yes to both, most of the time. The wifi is slow in the evening when the whole village is on it.

items.q: Can you cook vegetarian or vegan?
items.a: Dal bhat already is. Tell us about allergies when you book.

props.title: Come in Kartik, when the mountain is out every morning
props.text: Tell us your dates and how many of you. We reply the same day, and hold the room without a deposit.

image.alt: Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre in the last light of the day

pages.title: Rooms
pages.seoTitle: Rooms and rates at Aangan Homestay, Ghandruk
pages.seoDescription: A twin room, a double with its own bathroom and a family attic for four, all facing Annapurna South. Dinner and breakfast included, from Rs 4,400 a night.

props.title: Four rooms, one view
props.text: Every room is on the south side of the house. Quilts are washed every week and dried in the sun on the roof.

image.alt: The corner double room, its window framing the mountains

items.title: The corner double
items.text: A double bed under the widest window in the house, a bathroom with a hot shower, and a low table for tea. The first room to see the sun.

image.alt: A wood-panelled twin room with a made bed

items.title: Twin rooms
items.text: Two of them, each with two single beds, hooks for wet jackets and a shelf of paperbacks left by earlier guests. They share a bathroom across the landing.

props.heading: Rates for 2083/84
props.intro: Per room, per night, including dinner and breakfast for everyone in it. No service charge.

props.heading: Extras, if you want them
props.intro: Paid when you leave, in cash or by mobile wallet.

items.title: Lunch at the house
items.text: Dal bhat, or noodle soup and Gurung bread.

items.title: Packed lunch for a walk
items.text: Boiled eggs, bread, potatoes and an apple in season.

items.title: Laundry
items.text: Washed by hand and dried on the roof, back by evening if it is sunny.

items.title: Cooking lesson
items.text: Two hours in the kitchen with Aama, then you eat what you made.

image.alt: A twin room with a made bed and wooden walls
A kettle on the wood-fired clay stove
The house at dusk with the mountain behind

props.title: Coming in Kartik or Dashain?
props.text: Those weeks fill three months ahead. Ask early and we will hold the room.

pages.title: Food and village
pages.seoTitle: Food, family and Ghandruk village at Aangan Homestay
pages.seoDescription: Dal bhat on a clay stove, Gurung bread at breakfast, and the stone lanes, fields and forests of Ghandruk. Meet the family who run the house.

props.title: A Gurung village that still farms, feeds and argues together
props.text: Ghandruk has a school, a museum, three hundred houses and more stone steps than anyone has counted. Stay two nights and people will know your name.

image.alt: The slate roofs of Ghandruk climbing the hillside
Dil Maya Gurung sitting on the porch in a red vest

items.title: Dil Maya, who everyone calls Aama
items.text: She has cooked for guests since 2069 and for the village for longer. Ask her about the year the landslide took the lower fields, or how to make gundruk.

image.alt: The family sitting together in the doorway of the house

items.title: Bikram, Sunita and the children
items.text: Bikram worked six years in Qatar and came home to rebuild the house. Sunita keeps the bookings and the bees. The children will teach you a card game called kitty and then beat you at it.

image.alt: People working a green field below a snow peak

items.title: The fields below the house
items.text: Millet, maize and potatoes, and mustard greens in winter. Guests are welcome to help at planting in Jestha and harvest in Kartik.

props.heading: What we cook
props.intro: Everything is included with your room except where a price is given.

items.title: Dal bhat
items.text: Every dinner. Rice, black dal, seasonal greens, potato with timur, pickle.

items.title: Gurung bread and honey
items.text: Fried flatbread at breakfast, with honey from the village hives.

items.title: Dhido
items.text: Buckwheat or millet, stirred thick and eaten with gundruk soup. Ask a day ahead.

items.title: Chicken curry
items.text: A village chicken, cooked slowly. Order the evening before.

items.title: Local raksi
items.text: Millet spirit from the neighbour’s still, warmed in the kettle.

image.alt: A kettle on a wood-fired clay stove
A brass plate of dal bhat with vegetable curries
Stone steps climbing through a mossy forest
Milk tea poured into a glass
Stone houses and a field

props.title: Stay two nights, at least
props.text: One night is mostly arriving. The second morning is when the mountain usually shows itself.

pages.title: Getting here
pages.seoTitle: How to get to Ghandruk from Pokhara and Kathmandu
pages.seoDescription: Bus or flight to Pokhara, jeep to Kimche, then an hour on stone steps to our door. Times, fares, permits and what to pack for Ghandruk.

props.title: Pokhara, a jeep, then an hour of stone steps
props.text: Most guests leave Pokhara after breakfast and are drinking tea on our terrace by early afternoon.

image.alt: Stone steps climbing through a mossy forest

props.heading: The journey, step by step
props.intro: Fares are what we paid in Bhadra 2083.

items.title: Kathmandu to Pokhara
items.text: Tourist bus from Kathmandu, about seven hours with lunch on the way, or a 25-minute flight.

items.title: Pokhara to Kimche
items.text: Shared jeep from Baglung bus park, leaving when full, usually by 9:00. A reserved jeep can pick you up from Lakeside.

items.title: Show your permit
items.text: At the Annapurna Conservation Area checkpoint before Kimche, if you are a foreign visitor.

items.title: Walk up to Ghandruk
items.text: Stone steps through fields and the lower village. Tell us your jeep time and Bikram meets you at Kimche to carry a bag.

props.heading: What to pack
props.intro: It is warmer than people expect in the day and colder than they expect at night.

items.title: A warm jacket
items.text: Nights drop close to freezing from Mangsir to Falgun.

items.title: Shoes with grip
items.text: The steps are slippery when wet, and polished smooth by the rest of the year.

items.title: A torch
items.text: For the sunrise walk and for the lanes after dinner.

items.title: Cash
items.text: There is no cash machine in Ghandruk. The nearest is in Nayapul.

props.heading: Where we are
props.address: Ward 11, Ghandruk, Annapurna Rural Municipality, Kaski
props.note: From the Gurung Museum, climb the stone steps and turn left at the prayer wheel. Blue door, stone terrace, a dog called Kalu.

items.q: Can a jeep reach the house?
items.a: A rough road now reaches the lower village, but it is often closed in the monsoon. The walk from Kimche is more reliable and much nicer.
Yes. Bikram or a neighbour will meet you at Kimche. Rs 800 for up to two bags.

items.q: We are trekking to Poon Hill. Can we stop with you?
items.a: Many guests do, on the first or last night of the loop. Leave spare luggage with us while you walk.

props.title: Tell us when you leave Pokhara
props.text: We will have tea ready and someone waiting at Kimche.

pages.title: Book
pages.seoTitle: Ask for dates at Aangan Homestay, Ghandruk
pages.seoDescription: Pick a room and a date and we reply the same day. No deposit needed. Call or WhatsApp 9846-218405 from 7:00 to 21:00.

props.title: Ask for dates
props.text: No deposit and no card. Tell us when you are coming and we hold the room. If your plans change, just let us know.

props.heading: Which room, and when?
props.text: Sunita replies the same day, usually within a few hours. Most people stay two or three nights.
props.services:
Twin room
Double room with bathroom
Family attic (up to four)
Whichever is free
props.success: Thank you. Sunita will confirm by phone or WhatsApp today.

props.heading: When to reach us
props.note: The phone is in the kitchen. If nobody answers, we are probably in the fields; send a WhatsApp message.

items.a: No. We only ask that you tell us if you are not coming, so we can offer the room to someone walking up the steps.
When you leave, in cash or by mobile wallet. We cannot take cards.
Please arrive before dark. The steps from Kimche have no lights.

props.heading: Or just write to us
props.text: Questions about the walk, food, a group or a long stay. We answer every message.
props.success: Thank you. We will reply today, or tomorrow morning if it is late.
